Directive DIRECTIVE_044: Canonical Sources and Unification
    Intent: Agents and operators must use the canonical doctrine template, skill, or CLI command rather than improvising a substitute or copying from a prior mission artifact, because older artifacts drift from the canonical surface and copying them propagates the drift. When a concept is found to live in more than one location (a split-brain surface), the correct response is to consolidate to a single canonical authority — not to add the same behavior to every copy. A documented CLI command that is absent from the running tool is a gap to file upstream, not an invitation to hand-roll a workaround.
    Scope: Applies whenever an agent or operator selects a template, skill, or command to accomplish a task; whenever a split-brain surface is discovered during planning or implementation; and whenever a CLI command documented in canonical sources is found to be absent from the running tool.
    Procedures:
      - Rule 1 — Use canonical sources: always use the canonical template, skill, or CLI command surface rather than copying from a prior mission in kitty-specs/ or constructing an ad-hoc substitute. Templates under packs/built-in/missions/<type>/templates/ are the single source of truth, resolved through the charter/doctrine chain. Prior missions are historical snapshots — they drift and must never be used as copy sources.
      - Rule 2 — Unification not parity: when a split-brain surface is found — the same concept implemented or stored in more than one location — consolidate to one canonical surface authority. Do NOT add the same behavior to every copy (parity); parity preserves the split-brain. Exception: do not drop a load-bearing invariant without a migration path proven safe by tests.
      - Rule 3 — Missing command is a gap: when a CLI command is documented in canonical sources but absent from the running tool, trace its source and file an upstream gap issue. Do not silently hand-roll a substitute. The gap record and escalation to the team are the correct outputs, not a workaround committed to the codebase.
    Integrity rules:
      - No agent may copy a spec, plan, or tasks artifact from kitty-specs/ and use it as a template for a new mission; the canonical templates are the only valid starting points.
      - Consolidating to a single canonical surface is the only acceptable resolution for a split-brain surface; adding parity to non-canonical copies is a red-line violation.
      - A missing CLI command that is documented must produce a gap report and upstream issue, not a hand-rolled workaround committed to the codebase.
    Validation criteria:
      - New missions reference templates resolved through the charter/doctrine chain, not copied from prior missions in kitty-specs/.
      - When a split-brain surface is remediated, one canonical route is established and non-canonical copies are retired or redirected — never augmented in parallel.
      - Any hand-rolled substitute for a documented but absent CLI command is flagged as a violation and replaced with either the correct CLI invocation or a filed gap.
